name: Iran APT33 — Shamoon / OilRig
author: Threat Intelligence Team
prerequisites: Email gateway logs for the hunt window available in SIEM
Endpoint EDR telemetry (CrowdStrike, Defender, or equivalent) active
Windows Security event logs forwarded from all endpoints and servers
Threat intel feed with APT33/OilRig IOCs loaded (IPs, domains, file hashes)
required_tools: Splunk or Elastic SIEM with email + endpoint + network log index
VirusTotal Enterprise or similar for hash/IOC enrichment
MISP or OpenCTI with APT33 IOC feeds
Wireshark / Zeek for HTTPS C2 traffic analysis

hunt_actions.title: Spearphishing Delivery Detection
actions: Search email logs for APT33-linked sender domains (e.g., boeing-hr[.]com, hr-wipro[.]com, oil-jobs[.]com). Splunk: `index=email (SenderDomain=*boeing-hr* OR SenderDomain=*hr-wipro* OR SenderDomain=*oil-jobs* OR SenderDomain=*netzero-energy*) | table _time, SenderAddress, RecipientAddress, Subject, AttachmentName`

Hunt for macro-enabled Office attachments delivered to energy-sector recipients: `index=email AttachmentExtension IN (.xlsm,.docm,.xlsb,.ppam) | stats count by SenderAddress, RecipientAddress, AttachmentName, AttachmentHash | where count > 0` — submit AttachmentHash values to VirusTotal: `curl -s 'https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/<sha256>' -H 'x-apikey: <key>' | jq '.data.attributes.crowdsourced_ids_results'`

hunt_actions.title: Shamoon Wiper Indicators
actions: Hunt for RawDisk driver loading (Shamoon uses Eldos RawDisk): Windows Event 7045 (new service installed) with ServiceName or ImagePath containing 'ElRawDsk', 'RawDisk', or known Shamoon driver hashes. Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=7045 (ServiceName=*raw* OR ServiceName=*disk* OR ServiceName=*eldos*) | table _time, host, ServiceName, ImagePath`

Detect mass file overwrite/deletion activity: `index=windows EventCode=4663 ObjectType=File AccessMask=0x40010 | stats count as file_ops by SubjectUserName, host | where file_ops > 500 | sort -file_ops` — Shamoon variants overwrite MBR and bulk-delete files; > 500 file write events in a short window from a single account is a strong indicator

hunt_actions.title: OilRig / POWRUNER C2 Detection
actions: Hunt POWRUNER/BONDUPDATER DNS-based C2 (uses TXT record queries for command exfil): `index=dns query_type=TXT | stats count by src_ip, query | where count > 10 | sort -count` — OilRig encodes commands in DNS TXT responses; high-frequency TXT queries from a single host to a single domain are a red flag

Detect POWRUNER PowerShell execution pattern (Base64-encoded, downloads from C2): Splunk: `index=windows EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText=*Invoke-WebRequest* OR ScriptBlockText=*Net.WebClient* OR ScriptBlockText=*DownloadString* | regex ScriptBlockText="[A-Za-z0-9+/]{100,}={0,2}" | table _time, host, ScriptBlockText` — submit decoded payload to hybrid analysis

hunt_actions.title: Credential Theft and Lateral Movement
actions: Hunt for Mimikatz or LSASS dump attempts known to APT33 post-exploitation: `index=windows EventCode=10 TargetImage=*lsass.exe* CallTrace=*MiniDumpWriteDump* OR CallTrace=*comsvcs.dll* | table _time, host, SourceImage, TargetImage, CallTrace` (Sysmon Event 10, process access). Also: `index=windows EventCode=4688 CommandLine IN (*procdump*,*comsvcs*,*MiniDump*,*sekurlsa*) | table _time, host, CommandLine`

Detect pass-the-hash lateral movement to adjacent hosts: `index=windows EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=3 AuthenticationPackageName=NTLM | stats dc(host) as target_count by SubjectUserName, IpAddress | where target_count > 3 | sort -target_count` — APT33 is known to move laterally to domain controllers and email servers after initial compromise

questions: Has the organization received any targeted spearphishing emails referencing oil, gas, aviation, or defense sector job opportunities in the past 90 days, and are those emails preserved for analysis?
Are macro execution policies enforced via Group Policy to block Office macros from the internet (Trust Center > Macro Settings > Disable all macros except digitally signed macros)?

Are offline backups of critical servers stored in an air-gapped or immutable location, and has a recovery drill been performed within the last 12 months to validate restoration from a Shamoon-style wiper event?
Are DNS query logs (including TXT record query types) captured and forwarded to the SIEM for all internal DNS resolvers?
Is LSASS process access restricted via Windows Defender Credential Guard or RunAsPPL, and has this been verified on all domain controllers and critical servers?
Are known APT33/OilRig IOCs (IP addresses, domains, file hashes) loaded into the SIEM as a threat intelligence lookup, and are they generating alerts on match?
What internet-facing systems (VPN gateways, OWA, remote desktop) are accessible by accounts that also have access to OT or industrial control systems, creating a potential IT-OT pivot path?
Is the organization's sector (energy, aerospace, defense, petrochemical) one that APT33 has historically targeted, and has this been formally assessed in the current threat model?
